content: After going through this process, I think Prusa should rework this whole section. START with removing the tension screws for the lubrication and leave those pulleys unattached until this middle carriage is set up properly. Otherwise, it's a comedy of belts  slipping out because they don't quite get in far enough to hold tension. Even if that means there's a little less play in the pulley system, it will still have more than enough bandwidth to adjust tension. And I also agree that maybe a metal part should be designed instead of plastic. It's too late for me on this upgrade, but I will appreciate the more robust part when I get a factory Core One L INDX next years...
So we're going from metal mount to plastic? Hope it doesn't fail.
Like Luis said, put the square nuts now. Mine kept slipping out so I used M3x6 screws to keep them in play. Hopefully I remember that I am using M3x6 here.
Weird that this uses a plastic toolhead mount, where as my gen1+ had a metal mount.. Hopefully it holds up
Pro Tip just put the square nut in now instead of that weird position it tells you to later

I only had M3x8b not M3x8bT.
Shouldn't matter to much...
